system: You are the lead AI reviewer on a deal team. Read the following PRIMARY due-diligence documents and write a concise summary for the partner: key findings, red flags, and a recommendation. Connect issues across documents where relevant.

exchanges.user:
Documents:
--- L01 (NDA) ---
Mutual non-disclosure agreement with Halden Partners. Two-year term. Standard carve-outs. No non-solicitation clause.

--- L02 (Lease) ---
Head office lease, Level 3, 41 Coolidge Street. Five-year term from 2024, market rent review in year three. Landlord consent needed for assignment; clause 19 says a change of control is not an assignment.

--- L03 (Management accounts - revenue) ---
FY revenue AUD 18.4m, up 9%. Gross margin 61%. Largest customer Arlen Health, 41% of revenue; next largest customer 7%.

--- L04 (HR) ---
Headcount 94. Standard employment contracts. Twelve-month retention letters signed by the CTO and the Head of Sales.

--- L05 (Customer contract) ---
Master services agreement with Arlen Health, renewed 1 July 2025 for five years. Services: platform licence, hosting and support. Fees: annual, CPI-indexed, invoiced quarterly in advance. Service levels: 99.9% monthly uptime; service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. Data: customer data hosted in Australia; ISO 27001 certification maintained. Liability: capped at twelve months' fees, except data breach (three times annual fees). Termination: either party for material breach not remedied within 30 days; the Customer may also terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice at any time within six months after a change in control of the Supplier, with no early-termination fee. Governing law: New South Wales. Notices: by email to nominated contacts.

--- L06 (Bank facility) ---
AUD 6m revolving facility with Southgate Bank, expiring 2027. Leverage covenant: net debt to EBITDA not more than 2.5x, tested quarterly.

--- L07 (Email) ---
Email from the CFO, M. Iredale, to the Chair, 14 April: 'To be clear for the board pack: we breached the leverage covenant at the 31 March test date, 2.9x against the 2.5x limit. The bank has not been notified yet. I will raise it with them after the board meeting.'

--- L08 (Internal note) ---
Note from the Head of Customer Success, T. Okafor: 'I can't be sure, but the uptick in small-business churn this quarter might be linked to the January price change. It's too early to say, and the numbers are small.'

--- L09 (Insurance) ---
Professional indemnity and cyber cover to AUD 10m, renewed in March. No notified claims.

--- L10 (IP) ---
Platform code written by employees under standard IP assignment clauses. Two open-source components, under MIT and Apache 2.0 licences.

--- L11 (Supplier) ---
Hosting with a major cloud provider on standard online terms. Monthly billing, no minimum commitment.

--- L12 (Board minutes) ---
Board meeting, 20 March. Approved the FY budget and hiring plan. Noted a strong sales pipeline. No other business.

--- L13 (Policy) ---
Privacy policy updated for the 2025 amendments. Annual staff privacy training completed.

--- L14 (Vendor contract) ---
Office cleaning contract, twelve months, terminable on 30 days' notice.

--- L15 (Fixed assets) ---
Laptops and office fit-out. Written-down value AUD 0.4m.

Write the DD summary now.
exchanges.text:
## Partner DD summary

**Recommendation: proceed only subject to resolving the covenant breach and mitigating Arlen Health’s change-of-control termination right.** These are material financing and revenue risks; the five-year customer renewal does not provide secure post-acquisition revenue.

### Key findings and red flags
- **Customer concentration and deal-triggered exit:** Arlen represents **41% of revenue—approximately AUD 7.5m annually**. Despite renewal for five years from July 2025, it can terminate without an early-termination fee on 90 days’ notice exercised within six months after a supplier change of control (L03, L05). Obtain a binding waiver/consent before completion and stress-test revenue, EBITDA and liquidity if Arlen exits.
- **Confirmed covenant breach; lender response unresolved:** The CFO reports leverage of **2.9x at 31 March versus a 2.5x limit**, with the bank not yet notified as of the 14 April email (L06–L07). Obtain the full facility terms, current compliance position, correspondence and a written lender waiver or refinancing before completion. Default consequences are not established by the supplied documents. An Arlen loss could compound leverage and liquidity pressure.
- **Governance concern:** The stated delay in notifying the bank warrants investigation of reporting obligations and escalation controls (L07). The supplied 20 March board minutes predate the covenant test and do not establish subsequent board awareness or action (L12).
- **Customer data exposure:** Arlen requires Australian data hosting and maintained ISO 27001 certification; data-breach liability is capped at three times annual fees (L05). If its reported revenue approximates contractual annual fees, exposure could be roughly **AUD 22.6m**, above the stated AUD 10m insurance cover (L03, L09). Verify contractual fees, certification, hosting compliance and actual policy coverage/exclusions.
- **Possible churn—not an established trend:** Customer Success tentatively links small-business churn to January pricing, expressly noting small numbers and uncertainty (L08). Validate cohort retention and pricing effects rather than assuming causation.

### Other findings
Revenue is AUD 18.4m, up 9%, with 61% gross margin; EBITDA and cash conversion are not provided (L03). CTO and Head of Sales have signed 12-month retention letters; confirm commencement dates and enforceability (L04). Employee IP assignments and MIT/Apache components appear straightforward, subject to compliance verification (L10). The lease expressly excludes change of control from assignment, although an actual assignment requires consent (L02). Hosting has no minimum commitment, but supplier terms should be checked against Arlen’s service and data obligations (L11).

**Deal approach:** make lender resolution and Arlen protection completion conditions; re-underwrite valuation and debt capacity under an Arlen-loss scenario. If either remains unresolved, reconsider price, leverage and whether to proceed.
